reason: Stock fell 12.8% on a wider loss, CEO change and guidance cut, but management flagged Q3 ASP and gross margin improvement, positive operating cash flow, lower capex and investment-portfolio monetization, so the negatives look largely priced in; no clear unreflected edge.

Raised outlook (H2 above prior guidance, GAAP profit and positive FCF in Q4, 15+ pts of gross margin from in-house OLED, tens of millions of dollars of FPV orders next year) looks largely reflected in the +19% move, while the Q2 profit was flattered by one-offs and Neural I/O revenue is not expected until later.

Guidance was reaffirmed and SHOP NOI is tracking to the high end, helped by cost savings and falling leverage, but occupancy and revenue assumptions were cut and Q2 had a $1.5M one-time benefit. The -1.1% move looks about right.

Specialty steel producer: order book up over 50%, bar and tube lead times extended into late Q4, price increases effective August with full run-rate benefit coming, record aerospace and defense, Q3 EBITDA guided up and no pension contributions left this year, offset by a melt utilization miss and the stock already up 7.2%.

A 35% two-day drop looks like an overreaction to a modestly soft Q2 (Adj. EBITDA $72M vs $76.9M) and a leveraged $205M USPP acquisition. Management reaffirmed FY EBITDA guidance, raised the fuel margin outlook, and said July trends are bouncing back, so some rebound is plausible, but consumer weakness and the implied H2 decline keep this modest.

Beat with corporate growth at 9.3%, FY guide implied above midpoint, buyback authorization raised to $200M at a roughly 16-17% FCF yield; the 7.9% drop looks like an overreaction to the seasonal Q3 margin dip and hospital-slowdown comments, offset by hospital-demand softness and leverage near 3x.

Record Q2 results and capital return hikes were largely expected; the -5.6% drop reflects guided Q3 normalization in TCE and terminal volumes, and large Unigas gains and buybacks at a discount to NAV offset that, so no clear unpriced information.

The record quarter and raised guide look largely priced in after +18%, but the second-half guide just repeats first-half revenue and leaves out the funding lag, the commercial hires and the pushed-out cell and gene therapy order. That leaves modest upside to numbers and some drift, offset by a thin margin and the risk of giving back part of the jump.

The 7.6% drop looks like an overreaction to weather-driven margin softness and a guidance raise that was mostly Flyover and M&A. Core guidance was reiterated, lodging pacing is strong, Tabacón is beating, net leverage is about 1x, and buybacks are ongoing.

The 6.3% drop already prices the guidance trim from "at least" to "approximately" $400M and the weak fresh-fruit quarter. The call's offsets are real but expected: fuel surcharges arriving with a lag, the $95M port-sale proceeds with leverage heading to about 1.5x, and a steady Diversified Americas. Neither side stands out.

The 9.3% drop looks overdone against record revenue, 39% gross margin, $93M cash and about $24M of post-quarter orders, so the backlog should rise next quarter. The negatives (NGSRI delay, G5 redesign behind schedule, flat sequential backlog, supply constraints) were mostly disclosed and likely priced in.

Guidance cut, volume down 5.8%, and next-year commodity and fuel headwinds. The -6.8% move covers the miss, but analyst estimate cuts and the dividend not covered by the lowered EPS guide ($0.75-0.85) probably weigh on the stock further.

Strong beat and raised outlook (occupancy, signed-not-commenced rents, 2026 growth) look largely priced in after the +7.4% move; heavy capex and leverage and the short-term retail leases offset it, so no clear unreflected edge.

Stock fell about 10% on a permit timing slip (no Q1 grant) and a decision not to extend the SPAC warrants. The call adds little beyond that. Cash is thin, with $143M liquidity and a 12-month runway claim. The Q2 loss was driven by non-cash Allseas charges, and management says it is not planning capital raises while it pursues government funding. This looks largely priced in, and I have no clear view either way.

Revenue and ARR guidance were raised and EBITDA margin expanded, but gross margin headwinds (more purchase subscriptions, Gen1 returns, component costs), ARR lagging unit growth and a normalizing revenue comp offset that, so the -2.4% move looks about right.

Raised sales and margin guidance, positive full-year FCF, and gross margin up 490bp point to a credible turnaround, but the +6.5% move already prices most of it, leaving only modest drift upside (EMEA weakness and a Q4 growth assumption remain risks).

Strong beat and Q4 guide roughly flat sequentially (GMV $450-455M, EBITDA $22-25M) look largely priced in after a +12% move; CAG GMV weakness and falling auction participants offset; no clear unreflected information.

Mortgage REIT with a large book value drop and a strategic review is already largely reflected; the +2.1% move fits, with offsetting positives (buybacks, repayments) and negatives (more downgrades, earnings trough ahead), so no clear unreflected edge.
Mixed call: EBITDA guide raised, ad CPM gains and subscribers up, cash strong, but the new CEO gave no strategy until the next call and the stock fell 5.9%, so the drop looks roughly priced; no view.

Strong bank quarter (NIM +30bp, raised loan growth and NII guidance, falling brokered funding, improving credit) with only a +4.6% move; the main offset is that the time-deposit repricing tailwind fades in Q4 and the expense guide was raised, so the edge is modest.

The -12.4% drop already prices in the main negatives: the comprehensive G2 financing has slipped repeatedly, another $120M convert was needed, SG&A jumped, and $200-250M of phase I capex is still unfunded. The positives are the Clearway offtake, Section 232 tailwinds and guidance toward the high end. They roughly offset, and the financing outcome is binary and unresolved, so I have no clear view.

Stock fell 17.5% despite a record contract and a raised Lightspeed outlook, probably on higher capex guidance, the GEO revenue decline and refinancing/Chapter 11 worries. The call gave no new information beyond what the fall already prices in, so I have no view.

Beat and raise (revenue guide 12-14%, EPS guide 14-16%) was offset by concentration in one customer (~37% of revenue), service provider revenue excluding that customer shrinking, and memory cost pressure, and the 10% drop seems to price those in, so I see no clear unreflected edge.

Guidance (EBITDA $105-115M, ~10.3% margin) was in line with expectations and already partly priced in the +2.6% move. The Q4 margin dipped sequentially, 2027 rate visibility is uncertain (CA and CO are about 70% of census), and the policy and AI commentary is speculative, so I see no clear unpriced edge.

Beat on revenue and EBITDA, raised the 2025 EBITDA target to $80-105M, backlog of $2.6B and pipeline above $14B, and secured Siemens turbine reservations for a second data center project, yet the stock slipped 1.9%. Labor cost overruns and lumpy Base Electron revenue are the offsets, so the score is only modestly positive.

Guidance was reaffirmed, but the quarter was flattered by a $6.8M tariff refund and a membership-redemption sales hit (a mid-single-digit $M shortfall), and management guides only a "measured" recovery. The -2.3% move looks about right, so I see no clear unpriced information.

Strong Q2 (revenue +35%, backlog +55%, AD&G backlog +100%, tungsten sourcing margin tailwind guided for the next 6-12 months) and the big prime interceptor flow-down is not yet in backlog, so there is further upside. The +11% move already prices much of the beat, and EMP margin problems, a GAAP loss, inventory build and a weak medical backlog temper it.

The +22.9% move already prices the Q2 beat and Q3 revenue guide of about -5%. Still-unreflected positives are the heavy buybacks (about 20% of shares retired), $561M cash against the stock price, and METHODIQ and SpoiledChild strength. The ad-algorithm fix is still unresolved and the Q4 guide implies a slowdown, so I score only modestly positive.

The call was strong (record profit, 28% ROE, Mercury ahead of plan, credit stable, AAA ABS). The negatives were already likely priced into the 10% drop: direct mail behind plan, a flat purchase-volume backdrop, ROE reverting toward 20%, a one-time earn-out boost, and higher delinquency guided for next quarter. That makes the drop look somewhat overdone, but the fresh information is mixed, so only a modest positive score.
BDC call is mostly in line: NII of $0.26 covers the dividend, NAV fell 2% on non-accrual write-downs, and the price was flat, so I see no unreflected information.
Record Q2 with revenue up 21%, EPS up 29% and record operating cash flow, but subscriber adds were in line and there was no new guidance or big data deal, so the +2% move already captures most of it.

Record quarter, a 15% distribution increase, buybacks, affirmed guidance and a pending drop-down are all public, and the +4% move likely reflects them; leverage is low (1.4x) but the facility is over 70% drawn, so I see no clear unreflected edge.

Revenue growth accelerated to 22%, Q3 guided to about 27%, guidance was raised twice, and buybacks continue. Much of this is already in the +22% move. The raise looks only partly priced in, and low coverage may allow some drift. Lower-margin new business and prediction-market concentration cap the score.

Soft June quarter (flat EBITDA, new customers -38%, slowdown continuing into next quarter) was disclosed and the stock fell 3.9%; offsets are the special dividend and Tether upside, so there's no clear unreflected edge.

The founder CEO was replaced by an interim, the September EBITDA breakeven target was dropped, and Q3 guidance was soft with no partnership launches included. The 12.9% drop already prices much of this, but the revenue ramp now depends on Q4 launches that haven't started and the earnings path is uncertain. The $45M cost savings and $102M cash partly offset this, so the score is only modestly negative.
Strong beat, guidance raise, and $60M+ AI data deals were largely priced in by the +24% two-day jump; no clear unreflected information left, and the unclosed AI deal is only upside optionality.

Strong beat (23% GWP growth, 85.9% combined ratio vs ~87% Q3 guide, record income, BV up), yet shares fell 6.8%, likely on softening E&S pricing, flat to negative property rates, a lower-quality reserve release and a CFO change; the drop looks somewhat overdone, so modest positive.

Q2 EBITDA miss (Odin delays, rig transitions) was offset by guidance for about 23 active rigs and a sharp Q3 EBITDA recovery, but Gulf conflict visibility, high leverage and Odin execution risk balance it, and the small price move looks fair.

Seasonally weak Q1 with wider adjusted loss, but full-year guidance was affirmed and the fall catalysts were already known, so the 8.5% drop looks like a fair reaction with no clear unpriced information.

Weak Q2 (net loss, negative EBITDA, cash burn, higher debt) was offset by Turtle Creek cost cut to under $800M, earlier COD, and a larger forward book. The +6% move already reflects most of it, and the near-term catalysts (MISO study, FID, financing) are binary and roughly priced.

Big guidance cut (about 32% at midpoint, to $375-405M) with new-award timing slipping and supply chain delays, but the price barely moved (-1%), which suggests the cut was largely expected. That offsets the strong liquidity ($684M) and 88% win rate, so I have no view.

The -4.4% drop looks like a reaction to one-time tariff-refund flattery and weaker underlying equipment margins. Component-cost pressure and the absence of guidance cap the score at +1.

The +42.6% two-day move already prices in the EPS guidance raise (cost cuts, margin guide up to 23.5-24%) and sequential improvement. Offsetting that, US revenue fell 24.6%, revenue guidance was only reaffirmed, and the high end of organic growth was trimmed, so there is no clear unpriced edge.

The 13% drop captures the production and delivery cut, but the call also flags a coming equity raise (liquidity only $3B, FCF -$1.5B, "select the right timing to raise funding"), no guidance, and possible AMP-2 and Midsize delays. The +9.6% move already reflects the main positives (construction ahead of schedule, successful refinancing, strong LNG pricing backdrop, FERC timeline for Train 6). The call adds no clear new information beyond that, and the remaining risk is startup execution.

Record earnings, TBV growth and a strong pipeline are offset by NIM compression, a higher guided tax rate (28-29%), stalled insured small-business loan sales and slow SBA volume, so the -2.2% move looks about right.

Solid quarter (EAD up, dividend raised, book value up), but the +2.6% move already reflects it. Offsetting items are a quarter-to-date adjusted book decline of about 2.3%, a larger ATM, and rising securitization costs, so I have no net view.

Positives (guidance raised 50%, $41.7M Navy award, cash outlook improved, possible 3x printer speed) look largely priced in; the offsets are an ATM equity program announcement, 200 kW commercialization pushed out, and Q3 revenue flat with the existing Navy work winding down. The -1% move looks about right.

The -42% drop already prices a $68.8M partner-related charge, CFO exit and no guidance; management's claims of isolation and indemnity recovery are plausible but unverifiable, leaving balanced risk and upside.

Q2 beat with stent graft and On-X accelerating, and management says it held guidance out of conservatism after a weak Q1. AMDS PMA is now in hand but the benefit will build gradually. The +3.6% move captures much of this, and leverage and negative free cash flow offset the rest, so only a modest positive tilt.

Record quarter and a roughly 12.5% midpoint EPS guidance raise, with a strong Q3 preseason and a near-record municipal backlog, drew only a +1.1% move, so some drift upside looks unpriced. Falling attachments margins, negative free cash flow and weak commercial demand limit the score.

Seasonally weak Q3 (adj. EBITDA $18M vs $27M, volumes -1.8% on warm April) is already known and offset by RNG ramp, credit-price tailwinds, deleveraging and a steady distribution; the -0.8% move looks fair, with no new information beyond it.

Q2 revenue was light because of Middle East delays and deferred repair and product orders. Guidance was unchanged but relies on a stronger second half, and the visibility and book-to-bill commentary is mostly offset by that execution risk. The -1.4% move looks about right.

Strong beat and raised FY EPS/originations guidance (credit strong, buyback, record profit) already reflected in the +4.9% move; offsets are a softer Q3 EPS guide ($0.43-0.48 vs $0.50), rising-rate pressure on marks and NIM drifting to ~6%, and provision benefits fading, so no clear unreflected edge.

Strong record quarter plus a large guidance raise (mostly Flatrock acquisition) and a raised organic horsepower target; the stock was flat (-0.6%), so modest drift upside, though inflation and growth capex are caveats.

Weak irrigation demand, softer Q4 volume, margin pressure and a one-time tariff refund flattering Q3 are offset by upcoming restructuring savings, the end of the capex build-out, buybacks and a slightly lower Brazil financing rate, so the -2.9% move looks about right.

Strong orders/backlog and cash flow are offset by management's flagged Q2 revenue dip (pull-forward) and weak Q2 GAAP guide, all of which the roughly -1.6% move already reflects; no clear unpriced edge.

The beat, the guidance and the debt-free balance sheet are real, but the stock rose 61% in two sessions and that likely prices them in. The guide was only modest (Q2 EBITDA $6M, below Q1's $8M), supply is constrained and the equity raise dilutes holders, so the next 20 days look balanced.

The guidance cut to $158-162M EBITDA, margin squeeze in Memorialization, weak engineering orders and CEO retirement were all disclosed and are likely reflected in the 13.7% drop; the DBE interest and Propelis exit are soft and unquantified, so no clear unpriced edge.

The 8.5% drop already reflects the one-off ~$19M loss on the Asian credit fund unwind, which is partly offset by solid flows, cost cuts and an open strategic review with no news, so I see no clear unpriced information.

Specialty P&C insurer: solid loss ratios and a 15% GWP target that needs a steep H2 ramp, but expenses are still elevated, growth is soft, the market is softening, and there is no buyback. That roughly offsets, and the +2.8% move already reflects the print.

Office REIT call with a guidance raise, strong leasing and a debt paydown plan, but a 1.3% price move already reflects the beat; no dividend until later and the NYC lease is still pending, so no clear unreflected information.

Strong contract and capacity news (212 MW, $8.8B TCV, NVIDIA anchor) is offset by no material revenue until Q4, pending debt financing, CFO departure and dilution risk, so the 12.7% drop looks roughly fair and I have no clear view.

A 31% dividend cut, a 60-65% AFFO payout and a reinvestment plan were already priced in by the 15.7% drop. Flat AFFO, a visible occupancy path and a stalled tenant sale leave only a modest rebound case.

The guidance cut (revenue, EBITDA, Kiwi II timing) and the 17% margin were already priced in by the -9.3% move. Offsetting positives were buybacks, strong free cash flow, and unchanged core backlog. A back-half margin rebound is assumed but unproven, so there is no clear unreflected edge.

Q2 missed and guidance was cut, but the cut already assumes margins stay depressed. Comps improved to -2.7% in August, and the company has a clean balance sheet. Against that, Q3 is guided only flattish, with recovery pushed to Q4 and dependent on October weather. The -1.7% move looks about right.

Strong quarter (record revenue, best EBITDA in 2.5 years, MOU keeping 50-75% of a major customer's revenue) is largely priced into the +16% move; the remaining risks (high leverage, customer revenue transition, pending Intermodal sale, fuel tailwind that can reverse) roughly offset the upside.

Regional Texas bank: NIM fell to 2.90% with management guiding continued margin pressure, which the -4.8% drop likely reflects. Offsets are strong fees, falling classified assets, high capital and M&A optionality. Net view is balanced.

The -6.6% drop looks like a fair reaction to the delayed CSU readout, weak gross margin and a new CEO's reset, which is offset by the SG&A cut of more than 40% and the stated path to cash breakeven, so I see no clear unpriced information.

The call was a beat-and-raise: EBITDA guidance went up and Q3 rental revenue is guided flat with Q2, up more than 20% year over year. The CEO said no mats are on data center work and there is no macro change. The stock fell 3.7%, apparently on lower rental utilization from project completions, a 19% customer concentration, and a drop in product sales guided for Q3. That looks like an overreaction to timing noise, so I lean modestly positive.

The +5.4% move already reflects the expected Q3 gas rebound and the 2027 free cash flow story. Offsetting that are the second LOE guidance raise, volumes trending to the low end, and the Grey Rock share distribution, which is a supply overhang.

Beat was flattered by a $10M one-time gain and $2.3M non-recurring NII, offset by higher provision and NPL migration, while the positives (core NIM +14bp, fintech ramp, flat expenses) look largely priced into the +6% move.

Steady net-lease REIT quarter (Core FFO $0.38, helped by a one-time $1.9M termination fee); no equity issuance, high payout, about 9.8% yield and a modest pipeline are already known, and the +2.8% move reflects it, so no clear unpriced information.

Q2 beat with sequential EBITDA recovery, reiterated FCF guidance and a strategic review due in Q4 look largely priced in after the +7.2% move, while high leverage, 2027 refinancing risk and paperboard tariff exposure offset them.

Agency mortgage REIT with flat price. Book value down about 2.5% quarter to date and swap roll-off pressure on EAD and the dividend are offset by high-teens levered returns and ongoing ATM issuance near book, so I see no clear unpriced edge.

Guidance raise and record earnings look priced in by the +5.3% move, and the call adds offsetting caution: margin to moderate in the second half, expenses rising to about $49M per quarter, and flat average balance sheet ahead of election-related deposit outflows.

The +8.8% move already reflects the NAV gain (+4% to $16.51), the new $20M buyback with a matching $20M Main Street plan, and the dividend held at $0.36. Against that, ANII of $0.33 trails the dividend, non-accruals are elevated (5.8% at cost), the $150M notes mature in October, and leverage is below target. I found nothing material that the price has missed.

Broad demand strength, contract repricing into next year, raised guidance and faster deleveraging look partly unpriced after the +9.9% move. Offsetting this, much of the Q2 beat came from metal-lag and scrap-spread gains that management says won't repeat, so the second-half guide implies a sharp EBITDA step-down, which keeps the score modest.

Q2 beat consensus, first positive adjusted EBITDA, and H1 operating cash flow improved $17M, yet guidance was only held with a vague geopolitical rationale and the stock slipped 0.9%. That leaves a modestly conservative guide the price hasn't credited. Flat product revenue and slow IntegriCell ramp limit the score.
